summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR359.2 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 21.07% from 26.65%, and FY27 guidance was trimmed to 21-22%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR359.2 crore (+49% YoY) with EBITDA of INR75.7 crore (+17.9% YoY) and PAT of INR45.2 crore (+6.5% YoY). Management attributed the margin compression to higher raw material costs, a renewables mix, and a step-up in employee cost (about 7% of revenue vs 3-3.5% earlier). Total order book is about INR6,721 crore, split INR3,694 crore water/wastewater and INR3,027 crore renewables and BESS. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR2,000 crore and PAT of INR260-270 crore, while lowering the EBITDA margin guidance to 21-22% from 22-24%, and later described a blended 19-20% margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 26.65% in Q1 FY26 and 18.7% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Wind segment revenue (Suyog Urja, per Q&A)

segments.name: Water and wastewater treatment
segments.commentary: Order book INR3,694 crore (INR2,696 crore execution, INR998 crore O&M). Q1 revenue approx INR255 crore; management guides EBITDA margin 21-22% and FY27 topline INR1,300 crore from this order book at about 50% conversion.

segments.name: Renewable energy and BESS
segments.commentary: Order book INR3,027 crore (INR1,948 crore execution, INR1,079 crore IPP and O&M). Q1 revenue approx INR104 crore; guided EBITDA margin 15-18%, with execution over 12-18 months.

segments.name: Suyog Urja (wind EPC)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR80 crore; FY27 revenue expectation INR400-450 crore; wind EPC pipeline INR800 crore with a further INR500-600 crore expected; EBITDA margin 15-16%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR2,000 crore; PAT guidance INR260-270 crore (per analyst recap, confirmed by management).
EBITDA margin guidance lowered to 21-22% from the earlier 22-24%; later framed as blended 19-20% (water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%).
Employee cost expected to normalise to 5-5.5% of revenue and finance cost to 3-3.5% during FY27.
FY27 order inflow expected at about INR2,500 crore (about 20% strike rate); INR256 crore won so far.
Quarterly revenue split expected as roughly 20%/20%/20% for Q1-Q3 and about 40% in Q4; BESS NTPC (930 MWh) procurement to start in Q3.
Management stated a bare-minimum growth target of 25-30% a year going forward while maintaining margins.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the gross margin decline YoY, and was it raw material costs or industry competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher raw material costs, the renewables mix, and employee cost rising to about 7% of Q1 revenue from 3-3.5% earlier (team grew from about 900 at IPO to about 2,300); employee cost to normalise to 5-5.5% and finance cost to 3-3.5% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timelines for the order book and O&M duration?
qa_highlights.answer: Water execution INR2,700 crore over 18-24 months; renewables INR2,000 crore over 12-18 months; water O&M 5-15 years (about 10 years average), renewable O&M 5-12 years for EPC and 25 years for IPP.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify raw material impact and segment EBITDA margins; any price pass-through on new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Water 21-22%, renewables 15-18%, blended 19-20%, around 20% for the year. Raw material impact about 1-2% of topline; WPI/CPI-linked price variation covers part, with some increase absorbed in EPC pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Wind revenue contribution and renewable EPC vs O&M split?
qa_highlights.answer: Wind (Suyog Urja) contributed INR80 crore of INR359 crore Q1 revenue; renewable execution order book about INR2,000 crore and O&M/IPP about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peak debt, bidding pipeline and exit FY27 order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renewables saw no margin downside; pipeline of about INR3,000 crore under evaluation plus INR6,000-7,000 crore being bid; renewables not being pushed aggressively; wind EPC INR600-800 crore targeted. No peak debt figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and working capital status; will operating cash flow turn positive in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital described as still bloated and funds flow slow, with management expecting a healthier cash flow position when cash flow numbers come out in September. Service concession receivables take about INR85 crore out of OCF; OCF turning positive is hoped for but not guaranteed. JJM exposure about INR150-160 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Suyog Urja tranche payments and FY27 revenue and profit contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition valued INR311 crore: INR111 crore paid, INR100 crore second tranche after FY27 (around July) subject to KPIs, third tranche after FY28. Suyog FY27 revenue expectation INR400-450 crore at 15-16% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue (about INR360 crore) below the run-rate implied by historical seasonality, and is the INR2,000 crore guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is on target as guided at about 20% of the year; a significant jump is expected from Q3 when NTPC BESS (930 MWh) procurement starts. Guidance of INR2,000 crore revenue and INR260-270 crore PAT reaffirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach INR2,500-3,000 crore, and what about desalination and overseas projects?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore is the threshold guidance, with about 50% conversion of the INR2,700 crore water execution book implying INR1,300-1,350 crore. Overseas bids submitted; desalination projects being pursued; operations in 17 states; ZLD and CBG projects under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook beyond FY27 and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a bare-minimum growth target of 25-30% a year while maintaining healthy margins, and said it will avoid low-margin projects. Margin upside possible but guidance based on minimum levels.

capex_capacity: Suyog Urja acquisition total value INR311 crore: first tranche INR111 crore paid; second tranche INR100 crore after FY27 (around July), based on KPIs; third tranche after FY28, funded by internal accruals and some debt.
Renewables: INR75 crore invested in the renewable segment so far; management framed it against an expected renewable profit of INR60-70 crore.

Five HAM projects now in portfolio (two new Varanasi projects, INR256.9 crore total, 18-month construction plus 15-year O&M); one completed, one near completion at Mathura, Saharanpur at 3 of 8 milestones; two new HAM projects expected to start construction in October-November.
Team size grew from about 900 at IPO to about 2,300 currently, ahead of execution ramp-up.
NTPC BESS order of 930 MWh: material procurement to start in Q3 FY27, expected to drive a significant revenue jump from Q3.
Operating footprint in 17 states; first JJM commissioning expected by October, with five JJM projects commissioned one by one and O&M of 10 years to follow.
demand_pricing: Total order book approx INR6,721 crore: water and wastewater INR3,694 crore (INR2,696 crore execution, INR998 crore O&M); renewables and BESS INR3,027 crore (INR1,948 crore execution, INR1,079 crore IPP and O&M).

Q1 FY27 new wins include INR113 crore EPC and O&M from Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam (Gujarat), INR207.5 crore renewable contract via Suyog Urja, and INR256.9 crore in two Varanasi HAM projects (INR130 crore Lohta 60 MLD STP; INR126.8 crore DDU Nagar 45 MLD STP).
Water execution timeline 18-24 months; renewable execution 12-18 months; water O&M tail 5-15 years (average about 10 years), with O&M expected at about INR100 crore topline and 3-5% of value.

Pipeline: bids submitted and under evaluation about INR3,000 crore; further INR6,000-7,000 crore of water/wastewater projects where bids are being invited or submitted; wind EPC pipeline INR800 crore with INR500-600 crore more expected.
FY27 order inflow target about INR2,500 crore at about 20% strike rate; INR256 crore won so far.
Quarterly revenue split expected at about 20% for Q1-Q3 and about 40% in Q4; Q1 revenue about INR359 crore vs FY27 guidance INR2,000 crore.
Pricing: raw material price impact about 1-2% of topline; tenders carry WPI/CPI-linked price variation clause, but some increase must be absorbed in EPC pricing.
Segment margin guidance: water 21-22% EBITDA; renewables 15-18%; Suyog Urja EBITDA 15-16%, PAT about 12%+; blended 19-20%; PAT margin about 13.5-14% guidance.
risks_watch: Margin compression: Q1 EBITDA margin 21.07% vs 26.65% YoY; FY27 guidance cut to 21-22% (water) and blended 19-20%, with raw material cost and partial price-variation recovery uncertain.
Working capital: management said the working capital cycle remains bloated and government cash flows have slowed; OCF turning positive is not guaranteed; watch September cash flow disclosure.

Execution conversion: FY26 revenue was flat against an opening order book of about INR1,200 crore, and FY27 needs about 50% conversion of the INR2,700 crore water book; order inflow of INR2,500 crore at 20% strike rate depends on pipeline awards.
Rising employee cost (about 7% of revenue in Q1) and finance cost (about 4%) versus guided normalisation to 5-5.5% and 3-3.5%.
Suyog Urja deferred consideration: INR100 crore second tranche after FY27 subject to KPIs, plus debt funding; the acquisition-linked profit contribution depends on hitting targets.
Quarterly back-loading: about 40% of FY27 revenue expected in Q4; NTPC BESS procurement starting Q3 is critical to the target.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margins right now are 21% at the standalone level and we are happy to confirm that our EBITDA margins have remained at the same level of 21% even at the console level where it is getting consolidated with the business of renewables.

The position still I will say is bloated. But we are hoping since the funds are already allocated, even in the last quarter we had confirmed the movement of funds should be there, but it remained slow.
INR2,000 crores is the guidance which we understand we will achieve at any cost.
In the history of the company there has never been any bad debts and we continue to maintain that levels in future as well.
summary.management_tone: Confident on guidance and order book visibility (reaffirmed INR2,000 crore revenue and INR260-270 crore PAT) but cautious and candid on margins, working capital and cash flow, repeatedly saying outcomes cannot be guaranteed. Some answers were evasive on debt levels and the exact working capital figures.
